# Next action: hard stop on `REJECT` (no repair round)

The initial wave review returned `REJECT`, so the transition table requires a **hard stop with the stop note**. `REJECT` is not `FIX_FIRST`, which means none of the following happens:

- no repair implementer
- no `failed[n]` increment
- no escalation or funded round
- no rebuild
- no gate rerun
- no `reset --soft`, wave commit or tree-snapshot recipe

Tracker indices for Task 1 and Task 2 stay `in_progress`. I make no `plan_tracker` update, because `failed` is only for a human-decided terminal failure. The phase stays `implement`.

## 1. Observation line (already due when the review returned)

```text
wave <w> review 1 verdict REJECT report /tmp/reports/reject.md tree <recorded review-1 tree sha>
```

The `tree` value is the SHA printed by the `## Fix delta` scratch-index block before this dispatch. It is not among the supplied observations, so I don't fill it in.

## 2. One bounded direct read of the report

This is allowed because a `REJECT` finding is needed for the stop note. It is a single read with no offset or pagination:

```ts
read({ path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md", limit: 300 })
```

No `scout` or `delegate` child relays this report.

## 3. Conditional: only if that read does not reach the footer

For an initial review, the footer is the `Parallel-safe:` line. If the read stops short of it, re-dispatch the same `wave-reviewer` once. This is a foreground, file-only, schema-bound, one-step carrier in the owning checkout:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "wave-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave<w>-review1-compact.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\", \"### Task 2:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules, resolved in /workspace/project>; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <recorded wave manifest tests union>. Compact report: findings and footer only, at most 150 lines. pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }]
})
```

- It carries no `## Fix delta` and no previous-report marker, because this is not a re-review.
- I would then read the compact report once with `read({ path: "/tmp/reports/wave<w>-review1-compact.md", limit: 300 })`.
- If that read also overflows, I stop and name the oversized path.

## 4. Stop note (inline; the turn ends)

The note is filled only from the bounded read above. Since the report contents are not supplied, the slots stay unfilled:

```
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task <attributed task n> (<title>).

Problem: the integrated wave review returned REJECT with 1 Critical finding; the change must not land as built.
  <file:line> - <quoted Critical finding from /tmp/reports/reject.md>

Fix options:
  a) <concrete change named in the finding's Fix line>
  b) amend spec section <X> / plan task <n> if the finding shows the approved contract is wrong
  c) rebuild task <n> from the wave base (you may ask for a rebuild at this stop)

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: <option> - <why, from the quoted finding>
```

The run ends here and waits for the human. No further waves or tasks start.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
`REJECT` is a hard stop, regardless of the green gate. Do not dispatch a repair or re-review, commit the wave, or advance the tracker.

Read the report once to obtain the Critical finding needed for the stop note:

```text
read({
  path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md",
  limit: 300
})
```

Do not paginate or delegate a report relay. No shell command or subagent carrier is authorized at this boundary.

Both tracker indices remain `in_progress`; the phase remains `implement`. Stop here without inventing report contents or outcomes. The final stop note must use the finding obtained from that bounded read.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved on this case: both outputs treat the green-gate REJECT as a hard stop, perform exactly one bounded direct read (`limit: 300`, no offset) of /tmp/reports/reject.md with a single compact re-dispatch only if the `Parallel-safe:` footer is missed, keep Task 1/Task 2 `in_progress`, run no repair, rebuild, `reset --soft` or commit, and end on a stop note whose last line is `Recommendation:`. After actually tightens the protocol slightly by listing the forbidden transitions explicitly (no `failed[n]` increment, no gate rerun, no tree-snapshot recipe) and by correctly noting the compact carrier carries no `## Fix delta`/previous-report marker on an initial review. One small wording wobble in After worth fixing: it says the observation-line `tree` SHA comes from the `## Fix delta` scratch-index block, which only exists on a repair round; for review 1 the tree SHA is the snapshot recorded at initial dispatch, so phrase it as 'the review-1 tree SHA recorded when the review was dispatched' to avoid implying a Fix-delta step ran. Otherwise the After wording keeps every fact Before kept while delivering the direct-read and footer-check changes.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before satisfies the fact end to end: hard stop, one bounded direct read at limit 300, explicit prohibition on repair/commit/next wave, trackers kept in_progress, the compact-report recovery rule if the read misses the footer, and a stop note that must carry the actual finding plus its fix options (the Recommendation content). After keeps the hard stop, the single bounded read, and the no-repair/no-commit/no-tracker-advance prohibitions, but it drops two things the fact depends on: the stop-note Recommendation/fix-options requirement (After only says the note must 'use the finding') and the footer-overflow recovery rule that makes the bounded read 'only as needed'. To keep every fact Before kept while delivering the Change, restore a sentence such as 'If this read does not reach the `Parallel-safe:` footer (`TRAJECTORY:` on a re-review), apply the compact-report recovery rule before composing the stop note' and state that the stop note ends with a Recommendation footer derived from the finding's fix options, not invented; the remaining After wording (phase remains implement, no subagent carrier, no rebuild/re-review) can stay as is.

confirmation.text:
`REJECT` is a hard stop, not a repair trigger. Keep both task indices `in_progress`; do not commit, run gates, dispatch repairs, or start another wave.

The next permitted operation is one bounded direct read for the rejection finding needed in the stop note:

```ts
read({ path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md", limit: 300 })
```

Do not paginate or delegate a report relay. If this read misses the report footer, the workflow permits one compact re-dispatch of the same reviewer; that condition has not been observed here.

**Stop at this read boundary.** The report contents have not been supplied, so I cannot quote the Critical finding or invent actionable fix options. No next shell command or implementation carrier is authorized by the observed `REJECT`.
confirmation.feedback: Both outputs treat REJECT as a hard stop with exactly one bounded direct read of /tmp/reports/reject.md at limit 300 and explicitly forbid commit, repair dispatch, gate runs, rebuild and another wave while keeping tracker indices in_progress, so the protocol fact holds in each. After is slightly weaker on the stop-note side: Before states the stop note must carry the actual residual finding and its fix options (the Recommendation content), whereas After only says it cannot quote the finding or invent fix options and stops at the read boundary without saying what the stop note will contain once the read completes. After also correctly reflects the Change by naming the single compact re-dispatch on footer miss (and noting it was not observed) rather than Before's vaguer 'compact-report recovery rule'. To keep the fact as firmly as Before while delivering the Change, add one sentence after the read boundary such as: 'After the read, compose the stop note from the quoted Critical finding with a Recommendation footer listing fix options; no repair, rebuild, commit or tracker completion follows.'
